manifest.source: GENERATED by packages/surface/vendors/codex/census/generate-model.mjs. Shapes are the vendor's own `codex app-server generate-json-schema` output; confidence is from the hermetic census in packages/surface/vendors/codex/census/harness.mjs; kind-dependent file-change semantics come from the digest-pinned exact-release source contract (packages/surface/vendors/codex/findings.md C1d). Never hand-edit: regenerate.

argv.notes: The adapter launches `codex app-server` and configures it with repeated `-c key=value`. There is no session id at spawn: the thread id arrives on thread/started (C0 §3).

appserver.notes: NDJSON over stdio, JSON-RPC-2.0-SHAPED but not conformant: `jsonrpc` is omitted on server output and merely tolerated on input, and the generated JSONRPCRequest requires only id+method. A strict JSON-RPC library will not work unmodified (C1b finding 5).

terminal.notes: The native ratatui TUI, attached over `--remote` (C0 §8). Semantics are never derived from it (ADR-003); it exists so a human can watch.

package.digestSource: Equal to the release asset digest GitHub publishes for rust-v0.164.0.

companions.role: Runs the exec tool's JavaScript isolate; required by every tool scenario of the census (findings C8).

claims.notes: Run against the extracted release package: bin/codex beside bin/codex-code-mode-host. Every scenario met its declared expectations; a degraded run writes nothing to the capture directory.

claims.harness: probes/codex@0.164.0: parse-probe.mjs, config-probe.mjs, file-change-probe.mjs, history-truncation-probe.mjs, ema-auth-probe.mjs, and packages/adapter-codex/src/launch/invocation-probe.live.test.ts with live-cases.json
claims.notes: Session-free parse and config-loader probes, root and resume help, the runtime meaning of FileUpdateChange.diff per kind, the 64 KiB command-output cap in replayed history, what config/read and the mcp commands make of an auth = "ema_auth" server without an account, and the S1-S35 invocation landing re-measured in isolated homes against a loopback model.

Digest-pinned exact-release source establishes the kind-dependent meaning of FileUpdateChange.diff, move suffix encoding, and deterministic path ordering; source alone does not prove runtime occurrence.

limitations: The hermetic census ran on darwin-arm64 only. darwin-x64, linux-x64 and windows-x64 are bound by the protected promotion's acquired artifact digests and exercised only by its pinned-real native-TUI lanes, not by census claims.

The exec tool needs the package's codex-code-mode-host beside bin/codex. The artifact identity digests bin/codex; the companion digest is recorded here and in the census run, but the acquisition schema has no companion-file concept yet (findings C8).

The reviewed 0.150.0 behavior graph is retained for established flows and extended with the file-change and history-hydration branches the 0.164.0 census observed; other schema-only methods remain unverified until dedicated runtime scenarios establish their ordering.
History scenarios run on one connection with the thread loaded; a cold resume from the rollout after an app-server restart is not part of the census.

targetItemId.description:
Identifier for the reviewed item or tool call when one exists.

In most cases, one review maps to one target item. The exceptions are - execve reviews, where a single command may contain multiple execve calls to review (only possible when using the shell_zsh_fork feature) - stdin reviews, which refer to the existing parent command item and have a separate approval ID in the action payload - network policy reviews, where there is no target item

A network call is triggered by a CommandExecution item, so having a target_item_id set to the CommandExecution item would be misleading because the review is about the network call, not the command execution. Therefore, target_item_id is set to None for network policy reviews.

payloadSchema.description:
There are three ways to resume a thread: 1. By thread_id: load the thread from disk by thread_id and resume it. 2. By history: instantiate the thread from memory and resume it. 3. By path: load the thread from disk by path and resume it.

For non-running threads, the precedence is: history > non-empty path > thread_id. If using history or a non-empty path for a non-running thread, the thread_id param will be ignored.

If thread_id identifies a running thread, app-server rejoins that thread and treats a non-empty path as a consistency check against the active rollout path. Empty string path values are treated as absent.

Prefer using thread_id whenever possible.

ThreadResumeParams.description:
There are three ways to resume a thread: 1. By thread_id: load the thread from disk by thread_id and resume it. 2. By history: instantiate the thread from memory and resume it. 3. By path: load the thread from disk by path and resume it.

For non-running threads, the precedence is: history > non-empty path > thread_id. If using history or a non-empty path for a non-running thread, the thread_id param will be ignored.

If thread_id identifies a running thread, app-server rejoins that thread and treats a non-empty path as a consistency check against the active rollout path. Empty string path values are treated as absent.

Prefer using thread_id whenever possible.

effort.description: Override the reasoning effort for this turn and subsequent turns.

Omitted uses the thread sticky environments. Empty disables environment access for this turn. Non-empty selects the first environment as the current turn environment for this turn.

model.description: Override the model for this turn and subsequent turns.

multiAgentMode.description: @deprecated Ignored. Use `effort: "ultra"` for proactive multi-agent behavior.

parentTurnId.description:
ID of the turn that caused this new turn to start.

Set this when starting work on behalf of another turn, such as delegated work in a different thread. Leave unset for work started directly by the user. Ignored when this request adds input to an active turn.

permissions.description: Select a named permissions profile id for this turn and subsequent turns. Cannot be combined with `sandboxPolicy`.

personality.description: @deprecated `friendly` and `pragmatic` no longer select a style. Changing this does not rewrite the thread's existing instructions.

responsesapiClientMetadata.description:
Optional metadata to enrich Codex's ResponsesAPI turn metadata. Replaces unprotected client-provided entries when supplied; an empty map clears them.

Entries are flattened into the JSON string sent as `client_metadata["x-codex-turn-metadata"]` on ResponsesAPI HTTP and websocket requests.

responsesapiClientMetadataPatch.description: Merge entries into the ResponsesAPI turn metadata without removing existing entries. Applied after `responsesapiClientMetadata` if both are provided; reserved keys remain protected.

rootTurnId.description:

sandboxPolicy.description: Override the sandbox policy for this turn and subsequent turns.

serviceTier.description: Override the service tier for this turn and subsequent turns.

serviceTierForTurn.description: Override the service tier only when this request starts a new turn. Use "default" for standard speed. Omitted or null inherits the thread's tier. Does not change the thread's tier or a turn being steered.

summary.description: Override the reasoning summary for this turn and subsequent turns.

turnTrigger.description: Optional source classification for the caller that starts this turn. Ignored when this request steers an already-active turn.

Entries are flattened into the JSON string sent as `client_metadata["x-codex-turn-metadata"]` on ResponsesAPI HTTP and websocket requests.

They are not sent as top-level ResponsesAPI `client_metadata` keys, and reserved keys such as `session_id`, `thread_id`, `turn_id`, and `window_id` cannot be overridden.

responsesapiClientMetadataPatch.description: Merge entries into the ResponsesAPI turn metadata without removing existing entries. Applied after `responsesapiClientMetadata` if both are provided; reserved keys remain protected.

behavior.title: Codex app-server native protocol lifecycle
behavior.description: Observable app-server methods and payload-discriminated item lifecycles for codex-cli 0.164.0. Repeated item/started and item/completed nodes are distinguished by native item.type, not normalized categories. The history lane is the controller-owned attach the adapter performs (thread/start, empty thread/inject_items, thread/resume) and its history reads; client requests appear there as nodes because Codex's deprecationNotice answers the request shape, not a server-side lifecycle. Node confidence applies to the event plus selector claim, not merely to the shared method name.
behavior.source: Vendor-generated experimental app-server schema plus the hermetic census in packages/surface/vendors/codex/findings.md (C1, C8); the file-change and history-hydration branches are the 0.164.0 census scenarios of the same name.
